newsitem.title: GREECE: Intl investors offered more equity in Greek OTE.
newsitem.headline: Intl investors offered more equity in Greek OTE.

text.p: Greece's telecoms OTE has unveiled ambitious plans to raise substantial equity through a 7.5 percent rights issue, along with a part-flotation which includes a private placement and a public offering.

Some 15 months after its 96 billion drachma ($348.6 million) IPO which preceded its listing on the Athens bourse, OTE is tapping international capital markets again for an amount estimated in excess of 200 billion drachmas ($726.2 million).

The Greek state, currently the owner of 92.43 percent of OTE's share capital, is offering a total of 45 million shares -- 10.7 percent -- through a public offering and a private placement with international institutional investors.
Global coordinators - lead underwriters to the privately placed international offer are National Bank of Greece, Salomon Brothers International Ltd and HSBC Investment Banking.
Alpha Credit Bank, Agricultural Bank, Ionian Bank, ErgoBank and Commercial Bank have been selected as lead underwriters to the public offering.
A large number of Greek and foreign credit institutions, securities and financial services firms are also co-underwriting the public offer.
The private placement calls for a book-building process which will last between June 9-13.
Bids may be placed in a number of ways: total value, number of shares and/or share price, the OTE prospectus said.
The strike price shall be set between June 14-15 and investors are offered a choice between receiving their allocation in Global Depositary Shares (GDS) or common registered depositary certificates.
Depending on demand conditions, the Greek State may increase the size of the offering by 2,109,977 shares and global coordinators may allocate an extra 6.33 million shares at their discretion.
Subscriptions for the publicly offered tranche will last between June 11-13 with an indicative price range expected to be announced late on June 10.
The issue price will be 200 drachmas lower than the strike price that will emerge via the book-building process for the private placement.

Subscribers to the public offering, retail or institutional, are ensured an allocation of up to 100 shares, but a lower allocation may come about if the value of total shares demanded exceeds 100 billion drachmas, OTE said.
OTE will also seek to raise an estimated 200 billion drachmas through a rights issue, entitling existing shareholders to six new shares per 80 outstanding -- a total issue of 31,649,915 shares.

The Greek State offers retail investors with small shareholdings -- less than 100 shares -- the option to purchase up to an additional four shares in order to acquire a minimum trading lot of ten shares.
The rights issue price will be set at a 16 percent discount to the closing price of OTE's shares on June 13, rounded to the nearest 100 drachmas.
This issue price is expected to be approved by an extraordinary shareholders meeting scheduled for June 14. It will be made public on the following day.
The last cum-rights date for OTE's shares is June 17.
Rights will be traded between June 18 and July 18.
New shares arising from the rights issue will be entitled to a full fiscal 1997 dividend.
The Greek State has committed to fully exercise its rights.
It will also place privately with OTE's staff and pensioners rights corresponding to 3.0 million shares.
Following the part-flotation and the share capital increase, the Greek State will hold around 80 percent of OTE's shares from 92.43 percent today.
According to legislation, its stake may not fall below 75 percent.
Last year OTE saw its pretax earnings rise 22.8 percent to 250.1 billion drachmas on turnover growth of 14.6 percent to 679.5 billion.
Management forecast profits will grow 21.7 percent to 304.4 billion drachmas in 1997, but this could turn out a conservative estimate, its managing director Petros Lambrou told Reuters.
OTE paid a dividend per share of 180 drachmas for fiscal 1996, up from 130 a year earlier and beating its IPO prospectus forecast of 160 drachmas.
Management says it will stick to a payout ratio close to 50 percent. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 ($ = 275.4 Greek Drachmas)
